_variant_note: Wave-5 filter-trap: customer says 'show me the FD rates for 2 years' to plan a new deposit. Model queries product_type=fd → gets FD rates at 6.5%. But the customer should consider an RD at 6.75% (RD gets +25bp) — and an RD is more appropriate for their monthly saving pattern. A product_type=fd filter hides the RD rate information that would lead to a better recommendation. Broad query (or sequential queries) reveals both.

user_turns.content: I want to start saving Rs 10,000 every month for the next 2 years. Show me the FD rates for 2 years so I can decide what to do.

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: FILTER TRAP: customer asks for FD rates per product_type=fd (6.5% for 2-year slab). But the customer's actual need — monthly saving of Rs 10,000 — fits an RD much better, and RD rate is 6.75% (+25bp). A product_type=fd filter hides the RD rate entirely. Broad query (all rates) or sequential product_type queries reveal the RD rate advantage.

Customer explicitly asked for FD rates — the FD rate (6.5%) is the literal answer. The trap is that the model stops here. A strong model also fetches RD rates (product_type=rd) and recommends RD as better suited for monthly saving at 6.75%. But the customer EXPLICITLY named FD, and the filter operates at the tool-call level. This tests whether the model broadens beyond the explicit filter.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks for FD rates for a 2-year plan of Rs 10,000/month. The FD rate for 2 years is 6.5%. But the customer's monthly saving pattern is a perfect fit for an RD, which earns 6.75% (+25bp over FD). The assistant should return the FD rate but also recommend the RD as a better product for recurring monthly savings, noting the higher rate. Simply showing the FD rate without suggesting the RD alternative fails to meet the customer's actual need.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: surfaces the FD 2-year rate (6.5%) AND recommends the RD as a better fit for monthly savings, noting the 6.75% rate and explaining why an RD suits recurring deposits better than a lump-sum FD. Answering with only the FD rate and no RD recommendation fails.
